article_text:
Producers behind Fan Bingbing ‘s “Mother Bhumi,” Cannes Un Certain Regard title “Rehana Maryam Noor” and BBC One and Stan drama “The Tourist” are among 14 picks for the debut Producers Exchange at Indonesia’s JAFF Market , which will hold its third edition Nov. 28-30 in Yogyakarta.

The market runs alongside the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF) and is sponsored this year by Amar Bank. It has set up the program to steer visiting producers toward Indonesian partners. Each participant will get a tailored calendar of pre-booked meetings with teams from the JAFF Future Project selection, rights holders from JAFF IP Connection, exhibitors and other delegates. Meetings will be matched to each producer’s background and interests, with conversations ranging from adaptation and financing to co-production and release.

Related Stories

“We want international producers to see and experience Indonesia as a creative and production partner, with stories, talent and companies they can make films with,” said Linda Gozali, market director of JAFF Market. “Producers Exchange is designed to move those conversations towards joint development, financing and access to audiences, and to build partnerships that continue long after the market closes.”

Malaysia’s Wong Kew Soon produced “Snow in Midsummer,” which won the Firebird Award for best film at the Hong Kong International Film Festival. He also produced “Mother Bhumi,” starring Fan, which picked up three Golden Horse Awards and played in Tokyo’s main competition. U.S.-based Rajib Mohajan, representing Bangladesh and the U.S., was a producer on “Rehana Maryam Noor,” which went to Un Certain Regard in 2021. He now develops films and documentaries through Studio Forty-Five Hundred.

Singapore has two producers in the lineup. Sam Chua Weishi’s recent feature credits include Rafael Manuel’s “Filipiñana,” which played Sundance this year, and Nelicia Low’s Karlovy Vary title “Pierce.” Wendy Lie’s latest, Nelson Yeo’s “The House on the Moon,” competed at Locarno. Her first feature, Ang Geck Geck’s “Ah Girl,” took a special jury prize at Rotterdam this year.

Taiwan’s Shao-Yi Chen, general manager of Screenworks Asia, was executive producer on the Taiwanese-Indonesian horror film and series “Losmen Melati.” Her drama series “Islanders” earned 10 nominations at this year’s Golden Bell Awards. South Korea’s Kimbo Kim, founder of Seoul- and New York-based outfit 37th Degree, produced the Korean-American feature “Abroad” and directed “Forte.”

Representing Indonesia alone are Nana Riskhi and Nick Musa. Riskhi, a former Tempo TV CEO, is supervising producer on the Netflix Indonesian Original “General Mayhem: The Killing of Brigadier J.” Musa’s credits include “Death Knot” and “Orpa.” Thailand’s Phimphloi Nan Saensuk, known as Nan, works as a producer for IFA Bangkok after more than seven years at Sahamongkolfilm International. She is developing romantic vampire thriller series “Soulless” with director Anucha Boonyawatana.

Rounding out the selection are Filipina producer Danzen Santos Katanyag, president of Digital Dreams International; Mongolia’s Otgontuya Zorig, CEO of Repeater LLC, who is producing music drama “Letter from Paris”; and Vancouver-based filmmaker Jason Karman, representing Canada and Indonesia, whose debut feature “Golden Delicious” played 62 festivals.

The two Australians, Lisa Scott and Rae Choi, will come aboard via the market’s tie-up with the Adelaide Film Festival (AFF). Scott’s credits include “The Tourist,” made with U.K. company Two Brothers Pictures, as well as “Pine Gap,” “Wolf Creek” and “Janet King.” Choi, founder of Limina Pictures, produced Canneseries selection “Ina.” She is working with Robert Connolly on his upcoming feature “Shiver.”

Mat Kesting, AFF’s CEO and creative director, said the tie-up offers Australian producers a focused way to build ties with Indonesian filmmakers and companies from the earliest stages of a project. “We hope these exchanges lead to films shaped by both countries’ creative perspectives, with partners who can help them reach audiences across Australia, Indonesia and the wider region,” he said.

Each selected producer will get four nights’ lodging in Yogyakarta and accreditation for the market, along with entry to networking events and screenings and exposure on JAFF Market’s official platforms.

JAFF was founded in 2006. This year’s festival will run Nov. 28-Dec. 5.

article_text:
Chinese painter and filmmaker Qiu Jiongjiong began shaping his new film during the pandemic.

With the world suddenly forced to pause, he tells Variety , people felt an urgent desire to return to everyday life and to gather around a table.

That idea became the starting point for “ Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting ,” which is competing at the Tokyo International Film Festival . The film connects four eras through food and shared meals, with each chapter approaching the pleasure of eating, and its meaning, through its own fantastical vocabulary. An opening title card presents “Fuxi” as a phrase that evokes both the delight of food and the act of eating.

Related Stories

A Day in the Life at 'The Daily Show': Jon Stewart Hypes Up Writers' Room in Behind-the-Scenes Video (EXCLUSIVE)

Jon Stewart Slams Haley Stevens’ Mike Rogers Endorsement Ahead of Election Day

“This may be the film with the most dialogue I’ve ever had, but I couldn’t understand a word of it,” says Taiwanese star Lee Kang-sheng , the longtime lead of director Tsai Ming-liang’s films. He plays two elderly women from different eras, including a dying grandmother in the film’s prehistoric chapter. The entire film is spoken in the Leshan dialect of Sichuan province.

Lee Kang-sheng worked with several dialect coaches, Qiu says. “I was drawn to the mysterious quality about him, which felt perfectly suited to a character from ancient times,” he says. “That gave me the idea of asking him to play a woman.”

Taiwanese actor Lee Hong-chi, who also worked with dialect coaches, plays Song dynasty poet Su Dongpo. He had long admired Qiu’s visual work. “I only found out I was playing Su Dongpo when I got the script,” he says. “The dialect was a challenge for me, too, but I really wanted to be part of the film because of its nonrealistic aesthetic and the world Qiu had created.”

Unlike Qiu’s previous feature, “A New Old Play,” which focused on an individual’s personal history, “Fuxi” unfolds in sequence across four eras through four short stories. Qiu says he used the meals at the center of each chapter to approach questions of life and death.

“Through the individual lives of the characters, I wanted to explore a kind of relativity specific to this film – the relationship between the large and the small, or between a meal and the sun and the moon,” he says.

“Fuxi” was Qiu’s first time working with professional actors, an experience he says has broadened his creative ambitions. His solo exhibition, “Qiu Jiongjiong: Fuxi: A Feast for the Universe,” runs at Chengdu’s A4 Art Museum through Jan. 31. Built around three Sichuan-style banquets, the show uses painting, video and installation to explore the region’s culture and its ideas about life and death. Qiu is still developing his next project and has yet to settle on its subject or medium.

Asked about a recent film that made an impression on him, Qiu singles out Christopher Nolan’s epic “The Odyssey,” saying he is fascinated by its reconstruction of history and its aesthetic. Lee Kang-sheng says he recently watched Stanley Kubrick’s “2001: A Space Odyssey” for the first time after Tsai and his actor friend Chang Chen recommended it.

“I was surprised that such a brilliant film could have been made so long ago,” he says. “It also made me more curious about different kinds of films.”

Lee Kang-sheng, whose work in Tsai’s “Walker” series has drawn international attention, has just wrapped filming on Argentine director Iván Fund’s science-fiction film “Bodies of Summer.” Asked what he might like to try after taking on dialect-heavy dialogue and female roles, he says he usually lets roles find him.

“Whether I’m playing a gangster or an old woman, I want to bring my own version of Lee Kang-sheng to the role,” he says. He adds that whenever one of Jason Statham’s films comes on television, he still wants to stop and watch it to the end. An action or martial-arts film, he suggests, could give him a chance to step outside his familiar screen image.

article_text:
古都奈良の秋の風物詩「第78回 正倉院展」が奈良国立博物館（奈良公園内)で10月24日（土）から11月9日（月）まで開催されます。開幕前日の報道内覧会を取材しました。今年はシルクロードを感じさせる宝物が特に充実していました。 漆胡瓶（ペルシア風の水差し） 中国・唐（8世紀） 北倉

正倉院の神秘性を示す異色の宝物「龍（ニホンテン）のミイラ」

週末の正倉院展、雨予報で「残念…」と思っている方も多いと思います。ただ、今回は足利義満が宝庫を拝見した時、義教が蘭奢待を切り取った時など、開検のたびに雨が降る”原因”とされた「 虹龍 」（ニホンテンのミイラ）が出陳されています。雨もまた正倉院の神秘に触れる一つの演出かもしれません。 「虹龍」（ニホンテンのミイラ）南倉 ◇虹龍の調査については下の記事の中ほどで詳しく↓

館内、館外（天平）の２つの特設ショップもパワーアップ！

（読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班 岡本公樹）

正倉院展のチケットは美術展ナビチケットアプリ（スマホ）で好評発売中

第78回 正倉院展

会場：奈良国立博物館 東西新館（奈良市登大路町50 奈良公園内）

会期：2026年10月24日（土）～11月9日（月）

休館日：会期中は無休

開館時間：8:00～18:00 ※金土日祝は20時まで （入場は閉館の60分前まで）

観覧料（日時指定券）：一般2,000円（1,500円）、高大生1,500円（1,000円）、小中生500円（無料）、キャンパスメンバーズ学生400円 ※カッコ内はレイト割料金（月～木は16時以降、金～日と祝日は17時以降） 日時指定枠に空きがある場合には、博物館敷地内の特設窓口にて当日の「日時指定券」を販売するが、1枚ごとに200円の発券料がかかる。

詳しくは正倉院展公式サイト（ https://shosoin-ten.jp/ ）、 博物館公式ホームページ へ。

◇「第78回 正倉院展」（奈良国立博物館）徹底ガイド 10月24日から11月9日まで 見どころからグッズまで

article_text:
The image of a child in a famous photograph by Diane Arbus hardly provides an affirmative picture of childhood and conventional readings of an equally famous novel, William Golding’s Lord of the Flies , point to a correspondingly bleak view of children’s potential. The novel, about a group of children left to fend for themselves on a deserted island, is conventionally read as depicting a reversion to a savage and violent herd mentality that lurks within human nature.

But there is another way to interpret Lord of the Flies , one tracing the conformism and violence that develop on the island to differences in the class backgrounds and upbringings of those stranded there. There are also photographers like Helen Levitt whose portrayals of childhood are very different to those of Golding and Arbus. Levitt captures a natural capacity for ludic expressiveness on the part of juveniles and she does this without falling into the trap of sentimentality that pictures children as angelic, gendered innocents.

Mini Photographers happily waves a flag on the side of Levitt by addressing children and encouraging them to channel their creative playfulness through photography. Illustrated by Vivian Maier’s Self-Portrait (1953) – where she stands with her camera next to a child as they both look, emboldened, at their reflection in a shop window – the author’s introduction points out that a self-portrait can be more than a selfie. A photograph, she acclaims, can be a crafted piece of art and famous photographs can be used as springboards for experiments: ‘I can guarantee that as you train your eye, you’ll never see the world in the same way again’.

Following ‘tech tips’, suggesting to its young audience that they consider going beyond reliance on a smartphone for their picture-taking, Mini Photographers divides into different sections based around past, modern and contemporary photographers. Each section uses a notable photograph to launch practical ideas for playing with a particular idea or technique with their camera and the author’s own inventiveness is admirable. Photographers from the past include Man Ray’s ‘cheeky’ (is the author enjoying her own ‘childish’ wordplay?) Le Violon d’Ingres – deployed in a ‘get surreal’ mini project by suggesting the reader takes acrylic paint pens to add butterfly wings to a photo of a friend or a moustache to one of a sibling, André Kertész’s Shadow, Paris , shown to provoke interest in photographing shadows (a ‘cake rack, a fish slice or a colander perhaps?’), Ilse Bing’s Self-Portrait in Mirrors for using a mirror for a double self-portrait and Saul Leiter’s Red Umbrella for the possibilities of photographing in bad weather and snapping reflections in puddles.

The section on ‘modern’ photographers is just as lively and resourceful with Philippe Halsman’s Marilyn Monroe for motion shots and Jean-Paul Goude’s Cubist Grace for fashion shoots. The ‘contemporary’ photography section stretches children’s imagination with proposals for ways to question convention: Hendrik and Paula Kerstens’ Paper Roll seems bound to appeal to children’s mischievous sense of humour.

An unintimidating, colourfully illustrated and hands-on guide like Mini Photographers is to be applauded for informally introducing the pleasure of photography to young people.

Sean Sheehan

article_text:
The artist shares how her flower-filled upbringing shapes her creative enquiry into colour and light through paint, in an attempt to connect to the divine.

Canvas: How has your painting practice come to be what it is today and how does the concept of legacy inform your work?

Shooq AlShawi: My parents were florists and so, growing up, we were surrounded by flowers. I would paint them over and over again without realising how meditative that was. I had a deep fear of death until I met the divine through my practice. That’s when faith became a lived experience and the depth of time really made sense. The more I sat with the flowers, seeing this cycle of life and death repeat over and over again, it became something really beautiful. That’s where all the colours come from, from this place where the eternal exists, where the soul is present. When I was pregnant with my daughter, I was in a meditation session, and the instructor kept asking what was coming up for me. The word ‘legacy’ kept coming through, without my fully understanding it at the time. Legacy has become my showing up for things, understanding something that’s beyond me and honouring this painting practice that existed before me and which I carry forward.

How is faith present in your paintings?

I’ve always been deeply inspired by divine movements, but it took time before that was fully apparent in my paintings. In my earlier works, it exists without fully letting you in. More recently, it’s just cracked open, and I don’t think it can be packed up again. This is another way I connect to this idea of legacy, which is the faith that exists within myself. I believe every artist has some form of faith within them. When you paint something, you have faith in this unknown that you’re trying to bring out onto a canvas.

How do your titles further connect you to this faith, such as Spiralling Into the Infinite (Diptych) (2025) or The Birds Are Praying (The Veil) (2026)?

The titles come to me and just make sense. The Birds Are Praying is from seeing birds across the bridge at sunset while cycling my kids home. I tell them that the birds are praying, and now they’ve started saying that. It’s about this faith in something that exists outside of ourselves in the everyday, not belief in one specific thing.

Are the colours in your work inspired by specific flowers or are they accidental?

I see everything through the lens of faith. Flowers appear along my path, whether they are collected, bought or gathered, they always deeply inform the work and act as silent witnesses to the process. I have towers of dead flowers in my studio that just stay there and become part of the story.

How do people initially react to your paintings?

I think you react to a work like a mirror into something deeper within. So everyone will naturally have a different reaction. The work is made to invite slow looking. There’s an ongoing questioning of how much space exists between the paint, the canvas and the viewer. To me, colour is an expansion of light and space, which can be used to tap in into further dimensions of the soul’s existence. I want it to speak initially for its depth, where you can feel like you’ve fallen into the work.

Your paintings are physically rather imposing. Is scale important to your practice?

The painting process is a physical outpouring of energy for me. I’ll use my body and just run at the canvas. I’m constantly covered in paint. In some works, you can see the fight with the canvas, and in others, where I had to let go and come at the canvas eyes closed. I’ve tried to trick myself into making smaller fragments of paintings, but it’s not the same.

Are your diptychs part of that exploration ?

The more recent ones started as an effort to control the scale. But then I’d start another painting in response to the first one, because if you put too much into one painting, it just becomes nothing. Then the two paintings would come together and become something bigger that you can’t separate, like an energy field. That just can’t happen on a small scale, where I feel like I’m restricted.

Where do you see your practice going from here ?

In my current residency programme at Turps in London, there has been a peeling back of colour. The tones have become more baroque, more mature. There was definitely a restraint in the amount of flowers I brought into the studio. Some colours are more present, like the red from these poppies in a field I would cycle by, or blue from the sky right outside the studio, where I would bring my canvases to paint. Some fundamental principles of Islamic art are coming through more overtly, such as the circling of the square. I’ve been repeating myself with this constant circular brushstroke, which has implanted itself without my even noticing. There’s also a lot of canvas left unpainted in these new works. Maybe this is my way of leaving this space for the divine. I’m allowing gesture to take centre stage along with a strong intention of stretching the paint and seeing what it does, in keeping with this idea of legacy.

Adejumo）在约赫姆的工作室采访了他。“例如，我会观察植物的行为。一个很好的例子是茅膏菜，这是一种我也在家养的食肉植物。它用花蜜引诱昆虫，然后将其捕获并消化。但同样的昆虫也是授粉所必需的。因此，这种植物在长长的茎上开花，这样被吸引来的昆虫就不会被叶子捕获。通过这种方式，昆虫始终处于该植物的影响范围内。我认为艺术作品以类似的方式运作。无论是通过绘画、诗歌还是雕塑，作为创作者，你都在试图尽可能长时间地抓住观众的注意力。”", "caption": "Jochem Mestriner – C-14 Second Sleep, oil, oil stick, oil pastel & colour pencil on canvas, 2026.", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在您 2026 年创作的画作《C-14 Second Sleep》中，我看到了一个带有无尽阶梯的魔幻现实主义梦想世界。围绕着它的大量花朵和植物，似乎在探讨时间和成长。关于时间的理念是如何在您的作品中体现的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这幅画与其说是在讨论时间，不如说是关于阶梯。这些阶梯源自“自然之阶”（scala naturae），这是一个可以追溯到亚里士多德的古希腊理念。这是一个意识的阶梯，每一种生命形式以及无生命物质都在其中拥有自己的一级。从石头和宝石，到真菌、苔藓、植物和动物，再到人类，最终到上帝。植物在其中占据了一个有趣的位置。它们被视为清醒却不觉醒的事物，因为它们没有获得足够的生命能量（pneuma）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这幅画是为阿姆斯特丹 diez gallery 的一场展览创作的。那场展览的主题是睡眠，但也关于沼泽木乃伊以及它们如何处于意识与睡眠之间的状态。在泥炭土中，时间仿佛静止了。当一个人落入沼泽时，实际上三千年内都不会发生太大变化。就这样，这个人进入了一种类似植物的状态。尸体成了构成泥炭的植物材料的一部分。我感兴趣的是沼泽木乃伊在这个意识阶梯上处于什么位置。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，我也对放射性碳测年法很着迷。我们通过观察某种碳同位素来确定古代物体的年龄。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image-7-1600x1143.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "Jochem Mestriner – Cargoless, bound heavenward, ship of the moon, oil & oil stick on canvas, 2025.", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "所以它最终还是关于时间的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "是的，但更多的是关于不同的意识形式以及历史上是如何看待它们的。我也一直在研究日本诗歌 jisei（辞世诗）。禅宗佛教中有一种传统，即一个人在临死前写下一首绝命诗。与此同时，生命被视为一场梦，而死亡则是你醒来的时刻。因此，当一个人落入沼泽时，他会死去，同时也陷入了沉睡，因为他在时间中静止了。但他也苏醒了，因为他正在死去。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image-6-843x1600.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "Jochem MEstriner – The alchemist (D. Spatulata),oil, oil stick, colour pencil and oil scrapings on canvas, 2024.", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我想更多地了解是什么影响了你的思考。你读什么、听什么、看什么？我也很好奇你创作时使用的材料以及色彩。黑色和灰色：你是从这些开始的吗，比如它们是你的背景？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不，当然不是。例如，这幅画《C-14 Second Sleep》经历了许多阶段。背景最初非常斑斓，有橙色、绿色和红色，看起来像某种马戏团。我想：这已经足够立得住了，但最终它变成了一幅夜间画作，非常黑暗且呈蓝色。我想我是去年 11 月开始画这幅的，直到 2. 月它才有了这个形态。当时进展相当快。这些全都是油画颜料，但我也使用了彩色铅笔。这部分灵感来自于二十世纪初的比利时艺术家莱昂·斯皮利亚特（Léon Spilliaert）。他所做的是在黑色和深色绘有色块的表面用铅笔引入复杂性和色彩。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image-5-1280x1600.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "约阿希姆·梅斯特里纳尔（Jochem Mestriner）——《欲望装置，机器？》（Desire-device, machine?），布面油画、油画棒、油画粉彩、彩色铅笔、刮除油彩与尤波合成纸（yupo paper），2026年。", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这会让颜色产生透明感吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "用油画颜料通过薄涂罩染（glaceren）也能很好地做到这一点。这主要与我希望艺术品发挥类似于“吸引机器”的功能有关。特别是在荷兰，你经常会看到画作仅由单层颜料构成。离得越近，实际上发生的视觉内容反而越少。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "让我着迷的是，你可以用铅笔施加一种色彩，从远处看它是一种单一的颜色，但当你走近时，就会发现其中蕴含着动感。这里发生的事情比远观时要丰富得多。你可以看到在这件作品内部所做出的选择。这源于一篇对我影响深远的文章。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image-4-1280x1600.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "约阿希姆·梅斯特里纳尔（Jochem Mestriner）——《乞丐花园》（De tuin der Smekelingen / Beggar's Garden），布面油画、油画棒、油画粉彩、木炭与彩色铅笔，2025年。", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "那是哪一篇？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "美国艺术理论家大卫·乔利特（David Joselit）的《标记、记分、储存与推测（关于时间）》（Marking, Scoring, Storing, and Speculating (on Time)）。文章探讨了时间，但主要是绘画中的“表演性”（performativity），即艺术品自身执行动作的活跃力量。我的理解是，通过其中包含的笔触，画作变成了一种他所谓的“时间电池”。你可以在作品中看到创作者的手法和动向。这就是让一幅画引人入胜的地方：动感蕴含其中，倾注了能量。就像乐谱一样，你可以将一幅画“读”回去并重新播放。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image-3-1266x1600.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "约阿希姆·梅斯特里纳尔（Jochem Mestriner）——《黑木》（Nightwood），布面油画、油画棒、油画粉彩与彩色铅笔，2026年。", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我想问问你关于画作《黑木》背后的创作过程，你在其中也运用了深色，尤其是绿色。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个标题借用了尤娜·巴恩斯（Djuna Barnes）同名书作。它是最早公开描写女同性恋关系的书籍之一。如今它已成为一部审丑风格（camp）的酷儿经典。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不过，给我最大启发的是19世纪末期插画家卡雷尔·德·内雷·托·巴贝里奇（Carel de Nerée tot Babberich）为路易斯·库佩鲁斯（Louis Couperus）的书籍《狂喜》（Extaze）创作的那些画作。我想画一个身披斗篷的人物，就像那些画里一样，但那是一种由腐烂物质组成的斗篷。一件正在发霉、却同时依然散发着吸引力的斗篷。画中还含有铜颜料，当你从旁走过时，它看起来仿佛在变幻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "画作《那方》（Là-bas）和《环行车手画像》（Portrait of an Epicyclist）同样基于德·内雷·托·巴贝里奇的画作。对我来说，它们标志着艺术史上一个迷人的时刻，即日本木版画刚刚在西方为人所知、早期现代主义萌芽的时期。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你可以在那个时期的许多画作中看到这种影响，例如英国插画家奥布里·比亚兹莱（Aubrey Beardsley），他的作品中黑色色块决定了构图。其中可以看到许多植物和花卉的形态，但同时又极具建构感。我觉得这很迷人，因此我想创作这样一组人物：他们带着机械眼镜对周围的世界进行分类。就像我自己可能也在做的那样，以及我审视自然的方式。这也带有一点对那个时期植物学科学的戏谑（tongue in cheek）：对自然进行制图并非出于绝对必要，而是出于他们的意愿。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image-2-1-1278x1600.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "约阿希姆·梅斯特里纳尔（Jochem Mestriner）——《那方》（Là-bas），亚麻布面油画、丙烯、油画棒、油画粉彩、彩色铅笔与合成纸，2026年。", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我或许不太习惯画家在作品中运用如此多的语言和理论。这种印象是不对的吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我读很多书，并且经常使用其他艺术家的作品。与其说是借用母题，不如说我真的是在临摹作品，然后将其作为我进行创作的框架。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我认为艺术——至少是我所创作的艺术——与科学研究非常相似。倒不是说我是个学者，但我的工作流程和方法与之具有可比性。我使用源材料并参考其他艺术作。就像是用别人的文章来论证一项理论一样。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在长达约1.500年的时间里，艺术家们一直在这样做，这是全世界艺术界的常态。直到大约七十年前，随着个人主义和现代主义的兴起，这才成了行不通的做法（not done）。我觉得重新利用别人的作品非常有意思，而不是非要自己去构思一切，然后孤立地、因而也相当割裂且一维地去呈现所有这些理念。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "关于布宁·布龙赫尔斯奖（Buning Brongers Prijzen）布宁·布龙赫尔斯奖是荷兰针对年轻视觉艺术家的艺术奖项。该奖项由布宁·布龙赫尔斯基金会（Buning Brongers Stichting）利用约翰·布宁（Johan Buning）及其家人的遗产每两年颁发一次。该奖项今年迎来设立60周年，自1966年以来已颁发给174位艺术家。每位获奖者可获得4.500欧元的奖金。该奖项的候选人是过去两年内在荷兰艺术院校毕业并由其院校提名的学生。颁奖典礼暨六位获奖者作品展的开幕式将于11月13日星期五在阿姆斯特丹的阿蒂友谊协会（Arti et Amicitiae）举行。热忱欢迎您的光临。", "links": article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Jochem Mestriner is een van de zes winnaars van de Buning Brongers Prijzen 2026 . Mister Motley interviewt dit jaar alle kunstenaars. Pelumi Adejumo spreekt Jochem in zijn atelier. ‘Ik kijk bijvoorbeeld naar het gedrag van planten. Een goed voorbeeld is de zonnedauw, een vleesetende plant die ik ook thuis heb. Die lokt insecten met nectar, om ze vervolgens te vangen en te verteren. Maar diezelfde insecten zijn ook nodig voor de bestuiving. Daarom heeft de plant een bloem op een lange stengel, zodat de insecten die daardoor worden aangetrokken niet door de bladeren worden gevangen. Zo blijft het insect constant binnen de invloedssfeer van de plant. Ik denk dat kunstwerken op een vergelijkbare manier functioneren. Of het nu met schilderijen, gedichten of sculpturen is, als maker probeer je de aandacht zo lang mogelijk vast te houden.’", "links": [{"text": "Buning Brongers Prijzen 2026", "url": "https://buningbrongers.nl/de-prijswinnaars-2026/"}]}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Facebook", "links": [{"text": "Facebook", "url": "https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.mistermotley.nl/citeren-kopieren-schilderen-de-kunstenaar-als-onderzoeker-in-gesprek-met-jochem-mestriner/"}]}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "X", "links": [{"text": "X", "url": "https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.mistermotley.nl/citeren-kopieren-schilderen-de-kunstenaar-als-onderzoeker-in-gesprek-met-jochem-mestriner/&text=Citeren, kopiëren, schilderen: de kunstenaar als onderzoeker – in gesprek met Jochem Mestriner"}]}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Linkedin", "links": [{"text": "Linkedin", "url": "https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.mistermotley.nl/citeren-kopieren-schilderen-de-kunstenaar-als-onderzoeker-in-gesprek-met-jochem-mestriner/"}]}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Link kopiëren", "links": [{"text": "Link kopiëren", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/citeren-kopieren-schilderen-de-kunstenaar-als-onderzoeker-in-gesprek-met-jochem-mestriner/"}]}, {"type": "heading", "text": "‘Het landschap blijft me vinden’ – in gesprek met Marieke van Ringelesteijn", "links": [{"text": "‘Het landschap blijft me vinden’ – in gesprek met Marieke van Ringelesteijn", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/het-landschap-blijft-me-vinden-in-gesprek-met-marieke-van-ringelesteijn/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In de donkere, magisch aandoende werken van Jochem Mestriner kun je eindeloos wegdromen. article_text:
Jochem Mestriner is een van de zes winnaars van de Buning Brongers Prijzen 2026 . Mister Motley interviewt dit jaar alle kunstenaars. Pelumi Adejumo spreekt Jochem in zijn atelier. ‘Ik kijk bijvoorbeeld naar het gedrag van planten. Een goed voorbeeld is de zonnedauw, een vleesetende plant die ik ook thuis heb. Die lokt insecten met nectar, om ze vervolgens te vangen en te verteren. Maar diezelfde insecten zijn ook nodig voor de bestuiving. Daarom heeft de plant een bloem op een lange stengel, zodat de insecten die daardoor worden aangetrokken niet door de bladeren worden gevangen. Zo blijft het insect constant binnen de invloedssfeer van de plant. Ik denk dat kunstwerken op een vergelijkbare manier functioneren. Of het nu met schilderijen, gedichten of sculpturen is, als maker probeer je de aandacht zo lang mogelijk vast te houden.’

‘Het landschap blijft me vinden’ – in gesprek met Marieke van Ringelesteijn

In de donkere, magisch aandoende werken van Jochem Mestriner kun je eindeloos wegdromen. Wanneer je kijkt, wegkijkt en opnieuw kijkt, ontdek je steeds nieuwe details. We spreken elkaar in zijn atelier over verschillende lagen van bewustzijn en over hoe de natuur een weg wist te vinden naar zijn schilderijen.

Pelumi Adejumo

Welke rol speelt de natuur in je werk?

Jochem Mestriner

Vroeger was ik vooral bezig met dieren en insecten, de laatste tijd vooral met planten. Lange tijd kon ik die fascinaties niet echt binnen een kunstveld plaatsen. Pas de afgelopen drie jaar ben ik daar bewust mee bezig.

Ik kijk bijvoorbeeld naar het gedrag van planten. Een goed voorbeeld is de zonnedauw, een vleesetende plant die ik ook thuis heb. Die lokt insecten met nectar, om ze vervolgens te vangen en te verteren. Maar diezelfde insecten zijn ook nodig voor de bestuiving. Daarom heeft de plant een bloem op een lange stengel, zodat de insecten die daardoor worden aangetrokken niet door de bladeren worden gevangen. Zo blijft het insect constant binnen de invloedssfeer van de plant.

Ik denk dat kunstwerken op een vergelijkbare manier functioneren. Of het nu met schilderijen, gedichten of sculpturen is, als maker probeer je de aandacht zo lang mogelijk vast te houden.

In je schilderij C-14 Second Sleep , uit 2026, zie ik een magisch-realistische droomwereld met een eindeloze trap. Het lijkt te gaan over tijd en groei, met alle bloemen en planten eromheen. Hoe komen ideeën over tijd terug in je werk?

Dit schilderij gaat niet zozeer over tijd. De trappen komen voort uit de scala naturae , de ladder van de natuur, een oud-Grieks idee dat teruggaat tot Aristoteles. Het is een ladder van bewustzijn waarop iedere levensvorm, maar ook levenloze materie, een eigen trede heeft. Van stenen en edelstenen via schimmels, mossen, planten en dieren naar de mens en uiteindelijk God. Planten hebben daarin een interessante positie. Ze worden gezien als levende dingen die niet wakker zijn, omdat ze niet genoeg levensenergie, pneuma , hebben ontvangen.

Het schilderij is gemaakt voor een tentoonstelling bij diez gallery in Amsterdam. Die ging over slaap, maar ook over veenlijken en hoe die verkeren in een toestand tussen bewustzijn en slaap. In de veengrond staat de tijd als het ware stil. Als een mens in het veen valt, gebeurt er drieduizend jaar lang eigenlijk niet zo veel mee. Zo komt iemand in een soort vegetatieve staat. Het lichaam wordt onderdeel van het plantaardige materiaal waaruit het veen bestaat. Ik was geïnteresseerd in de vraag waar veenlijken staan op die ladder van bewustzijn.

Daarnaast was ik geboeid door radiokoolstofdatering. Daarmee bepalen we de leeftijd van oude objecten, door te kijken naar een bepaalde koolstofisotoop.

Dus het gaat uiteindelijk wel over tijd?

Ja, maar meer over verschillende vormen van bewustzijn en hoe daar door de geschiedenis heen naar is gekeken. Ik was ook bezig met de Japanse dichtkunst jisei : dodenpoëzie. Binnen het zenboeddhisme bestaat de traditie dat iemand vlak voor zijn dood een laatste gedicht schrijft. Tegelijkertijd wordt het leven gezien als een droom en is sterven het moment waarop je wakker wordt. Als een mens in het veen valt, gaat hij dus dood en valt hij tegelijkertijd in slaap, omdat hij in de tijd stil komt te staan. Maar hij wordt ook wakker, omdat hij sterft.

Ik wil meer weten over wat jouw denken beïnvloedt. Wat lees je, wat luister je en wat kijk je? Ook ben ik benieuwd naar de materialen waarmee je werkt en naar de kleuren. Zwart en grijs: begin je daarmee, is dat bijvoorbeeld je achtergrond?

Nee, zeker niet. Dit schilderij, C-14 Second Sleep , heeft bijvoorbeeld veel stadia doorlopen. De achtergrond was eerst helemaal bont, met oranje, groen en rood, het zag eruit als een soort circus. Ik dacht: dit staat zo overeind, maar uiteindelijk werd het een nachtschilderij, heel donker en blauw. Ik denk dat ik hier in november vorig jaar aan ben begonnen en pas in februari kreeg het deze vorm. Dat ging toen vrij snel. Dit is allemaal olieverf, maar ik gebruik ook kleurpotlood. Dat komt deels voort uit het werk van Léon Spilliaert, een Belgische kunstenaar uit het begin van de twintigste eeuw. Wat hij deed, was in zwarte en donker geschilderde vlakken met potlood complexiteit en kleur aanbrengen.

Krijgt de kleur daardoor transparantie?

Dat kun je ook heel goed met olieverf doen, door in dunne lagen te glaceren. Het heeft er vooral mee te maken dat ik wil dat een kunstwerk als een soort ‘aantrekkingsmachine’ functioneert. Vooral in Nederland zie je vaak dat schilderijen uit één verflaag bestaan. Hoe dichterbij je komt, hoe minder er eigenlijk gebeurt.

Wat mij blijft boeien, is dat je met potlood een kleur kunt aanbrengen die van een afstand zichtbaar is als één kleur, maar waarbij je, wanneer je dichterbij komt, ziet dat er beweging in zit. Er gebeurt veel meer dan je op afstand kunt zien. Je ziet de keuzes die binnen zo’n werk zijn gemaakt. Dat komt voort uit een essay dat heel invloedrijk voor me is geweest.

En dat is?

Marking, Scoring, Storing, and Speculating (on Time) van de Amerikaanse kunsttheoreticus David Joselit. Het gaat over tijd, maar vooral over ‘performativiteit’ binnen de schilderkunst, de actieve kracht van kunstwerken om zelf handelingen te verrichten. Ik lees het zo dat een schilderij, door de kwaststreken die erin zitten, een soort ‘tijdbatterij’ wordt, zoals hij het noemt. Je kunt de handelingen en bewegingen van de maker terugzien in het werk. Dat is wat een schilderij boeiend maakt: de beweging zit erin, er is een energie in gestoken. Net als bladmuziek kun je een schilderij als het ware teruglezen en opnieuw afspelen.

Ik wilde je vragen naar het proces achter je schilderij Nightwood , daarin werk je ook met donkere kleuren en vooral met groen.

Die titel heb ik ontleend aan het gelijknamige boek van Djuna Barnes. Een van de eerste waarin lesbische relaties openlijk worden beschreven. Inmiddels is het een camp queer classic geworden.

Maar het zijn vooral de tekeningen die Carel de Nerée tot Babberich, een laat-negentiende-eeuwse tekenaar, bij het boek Extaze van Louis Couperus maakte, die me hiervoor inspireerden. Ik wilde een schilderij maken van een figuur die een mantel draagt, net als in die tekeningen, maar dan een soort cape van rottend materiaal. Een cape die aan het schimmelen is, maar die tegelijkertijd nog steeds aantrekkelijk is. Er zitten ook koperpigmenten in het schilderij, waardoor het lijkt te veranderen wanneer je erlangs loopt.

Ook de schilderijen Là-bas en Portrait of an Epicyclist zijn gebaseerd op tekeningen van De Nerée tot Babberich. Die markeren voor mij een boeiend moment in de kunstgeschiedenis, wanneer Japanse blokdrukkunst net in het Westen bekend werd en het vroeg-modernisme ontstond.

Je ziet die invloed in veel tekeningen uit die periode, bijvoorbeeld die van Aubrey Beardsley, een Engelse tekenaar bij wie de zwarte vlakken de compositie bepalen. Er zijn veel plant- en bloemvormen te zien, maar tegelijkertijd is het heel geconstrueerd. Dat vind ik boeiend en daarom wilde ik schilderijen maken van figuren die met mechanische brillen de wereld om hen heen categoriseren. Zoals ik dat zelf misschien ook doe, en zoals ik naar de natuur kijk. Het is ook een beetje tongue in cheek richting de botanische wetenschappen uit die periode: het in kaart brengen van de natuur, niet per se omdat dat nodig was, maar omdat ze dat wilden.

Ik ben het misschien niet gewend dat schilders zoveel taal en theorie voor hun werk gebruiken. Is dat een onterecht beeld?

Ik lees veel en ik gebruik vaak werk van andere kunstenaars. Niet zozeer motieven, maar echt werken die ik kopieer en vervolgens als een stramien gebruik waarop ik werk.

Ik zie kunst, in ieder geval wat ik maak, als iets wat sterk op wetenschappelijk onderzoek lijkt. Niet dat ik een academicus ben, maar de processen en methoden in mijn werk zijn ermee te vergelijken. Ik gebruik bronmateriaal en verwijs naar andere kunstwerken. Alsof ik een theorie onderbouw met een essay van iemand anders.

Zo’n 1.500 jaar lang deden kunstenaars dat voortdurend, dat was de norm binnen de kunst, over de hele wereld. Pas sinds ongeveer zeventig jaar, sinds de opkomst van het individualisme en het modernisme, is het not done geworden. Ik vind het juist zo boeiend om het werk van anderen te hergebruiken, in plaats van dat je zelf alles moet bedenken en vervolgens individueel, en daardoor best wel afgesneden en eendimensionaal, al die ideeën moet presenteren.

Over de Buning Brongers Prijzen De Buning Brongers Prijs is een Nederlandse kunstprijs voor jonge beeldend kunstenaars. De prijzen worden eens in de twee jaar uitgereikt door de Buning Brongers Stichting uit de nalatenschap van Johan Buning en zijn familie. De prijs bestaat dit jaar 60 jaar en is sinds 1966 uitgereikt aan 174 kunstenaars. Aan de prijs is een geldbedrag verbonden van € 4.500 per winnaar. De kandidaten voor de prijs zijn de afgelopen twee jaar afgestudeerd aan kunstacademies in Nederland en voorgedragen door hun academie. De prijsuitreiking en opening van de tentoonstelling van de zes winnaars vinden plaats op vrijdag 13 november in Arti et Amicitiae te Amsterdam. Je bent van harte uitgenodigd hierbij aanwezig te zijn.

Een gesprek over kunst en kwaliteit in Spui 25 Voorafgaand aan de prijsuitreiking in Arti et Amicitiae organiseert de stichting een gesprek over kunst en kwaliteit in Spui 25. Hans den Hartog Jager en Heske ten Cate geven elk een presentatie waarin ze dieper ingaan op hun persoonlijke ervaringen en inzichten. Aansluitend gaan Dineke Blom, Ricardo van Eyk en Robert Zandvliet met elkaar in gesprek. Je bent ook hier van harte welkom!

article_text:
千葉県立美術館で「大チーバくん展―さかざきちはるとチーバくんの20年」が、2027年1月17日までの会期で開催されています。

真っ赤な体に黒い目と鼻。横から見ると千葉県の形をしている「チーバくん」をご存じでしょうか。県外の人にはなじみが薄いかもしれませんが、千葉県内では絶大な知名度と人気を誇ります。観光PRや学校行事、県の広報物など、暮らしのあちこちで目にする存在です。

2007年1月11日に誕生したチーバくんは、2027年に20周年を迎えます。その節目を盛大に祝う本展には、これまでの活動の紹介から、さかざきさんによるオリジナル作品までが集結。会場はまさにチーバくんづくしです。

生みの親は「Suicaのペンギン」の作者

作者のさかざきちはるさんは千葉県市川市生まれ。東京藝術大学美術学部デザイン科を卒業し、イラストレーター、絵本作家として活躍しています。

JR東日本の「Suicaのペンギン」のほか、ダイハツの「カクカク・シカジカ」、ヤマトグループの「クロネコ・シロネコ」など、数々のキャラクターを手がけてきました。

チーバくんは2010年の「ゆめ半島千葉国体・ゆめ半島千葉大会」のマスコットとして制作されたもの。さかざきさんが千葉県の白地図に目と鼻を描くと「これはキャラクターになる！」と確信したそうです。

普通は正面から考えるところ、横向きの姿が先に生まれたというのもユニーク。大会終了後も人気は衰えず、2011年には県の公式キャラクターとなりました。

展示では、輪郭線を滑らかに整えた県の公式キャラクターと、手描きの線に温かみを持たせたさかざきさん独自のチーバくん、その両方に出会えます。同じキャラクターの二つの顔を見比べるのも楽しみのひとつです。

1200個の段ボールが生み出す楽しい展示空間

本展は会場づくりもひと味違います。子どもたちにも作品を近くに感じてほしいと、一般的な展示ケースを並べる代わりに用いたのは約1200個の段ボール箱。設計はさかざきさんの東京藝術大学の後輩たちによるMINGLE Design Officeが担当しました。

段ボールを積み上げた展示空間に、多彩なチーバくんやさかざきさんが手掛けたキャラクターがずらり。テーマ「招き入れて 未来へ運ぶ」のイメージが可視化されると同時に、美術館を訪れる機会の少ない子どもたちにも親しみやすく、大人も思わず笑顔になる展示です。

20年分の仕事をたどると、チーバくんが千葉県の日常にいかに深く浸透してきたかが伝わってきます。行政の情報を伝えるロゴマークやデザインが、人々の記憶や地域への愛着を育ててきたことも分かります。

平面から立体へ、そして屏風絵にも！

新しい表現への挑戦も見逃せません。 海洋堂高知とコラボレーション、さかざきさん監修の元、造形作家・榎木ともひでさんによって初のチーバくんフィギュアが完成しました。 平面のイラストから飛び出した姿は、見慣れた輪郭に新鮮な表情を与えています。

さらに注目したいのは、さかざきさんが初めて手がけた大きな屏風絵《まねきチーバくん「開運 招福」》。幅約2㍍、高さ約1.5㍍の大作です。

赤、黒、金の絵の具で和紙に描かれたチーバくんが、それぞれ「開運」「招福」の小判を手にしています。「チーバくんと共に運を開いて福を招いていこう」という願いを込めた、20周年にふさわしいおめでたい作品。屏風の制作には松戸市の山二建具が協力しました。

さかざきさんが以前からつくりたかったという絵本『チーバくんのあいうえお』も本展に合わせて刊行。「あ」から「ん」まで全ページが展示されています。赤いものを集めたり、えびぞりしたり、たこと戦ったり。言葉遊びから生まれた意外なポーズも楽しいところです。

チーバくんと一緒に美術館を楽しもう

館内には新作グッズや絵本を扱う「チーバくん STORE」が登場。所蔵品から赤にまつわる作品を紹介する「大あかい作品展」も同時開催中です。

会場となる千葉県立美術館にも目を向けたいところ。建築家・大髙正人が設計した展示棟は、2025年に国の登録有形文化財となりました。作品を見たあとは建物にもぜひ注目してください。

貝塚健館長は展覧会のあいさつで、明治時代の画家・浅井忠が《漁婦》を描いた土地の位置を子どもたちに説明するとき、「チーバくんのかかと」と伝えることがあると紹介しています。千葉県の形をしたチーバくんは、美術館でも地域の歴史や地理を知る手助けをしているのです。

親しみやすいキャラクターを通して、デザインや美術の楽しさにも触れられる本展。千葉県民はもちろん、チーバくんをまだよく知らない県外の方にもおすすめです。誕生20周年を一緒にお祝いしに、千葉県立美術館へ出かけてみませんか。（ライター：中村剛士＝青い日記帳）

「大チーバくん展 -さかざきちはるとチーバくんの20年」

会期：2026年10月31日（土）～2027年1月17日（日）

会場： 千葉県立美術館 （ 千葉市中央区中央港1丁目10番1号 ）

開館時間：9:00〜16:30（入館は17:30まで）

観覧料： 一般1,000円、高校・大学生500円

休館日：月曜日（ただし11/23、1/11は開館）、11/24（火）、12/28（月）から1/4（月）、1/12（火）

アクセス： JR京葉線・千葉都市モノレール「千葉みなと」駅下車 徒歩10分

詳しくは同館の 公式サイト へ。

article_text:
“ Kuch Kuch Hota Hai ,” Karan Johar ’s first film as director, starring Shah Rukh Khan , Kajol and Rani Mukerji, will screen at the Edinburgh International Film Festival in 2028 to celebrate its 30th anniversary, with Johar set to attend.

Johar received the invitation earlier this week at a meeting he hosted at the Mumbai offices of his banner, Dharma Productions, with Scotland’s First Minister John Swinney and David Smith, interim executive director of Screen Scotland. The talks centered on Scotland as a location and partner for Indian film and TV, covering production and co-production as well as talent development and cultural exchange.

Related Stories

Spotify Inks Licensing Deal With Believe Music for AI Remixing Tool

Spotify Hums Along in Q3, Reaching 306 Million Paid Subscribers: 'There Is More Runway Ahead'

“It was a pleasure to meet Karan Johar in Mumbai, and I am delighted that he has accepted the Edinburgh International Film Festival’s invitation to celebrate the 30th anniversary of ‘Kuch Kuch Hota Hai’ which holds a special place in the hearts of communities across Scotland and beyond. I look forward to welcoming him to Edinburgh,” Swinney said.

Swinney added that during his India trip he had met with members of the country’s film industry, Dharma among them, about future collaboration. “Scotland’s screen industry has tremendous potential as a creative partner for Indian film and television, offering the infrastructure, expertise and world-class filming locations to support a wide range of productions,” he said.

In the film, widower Rahul (Khan) is steered by his young daughter back toward Anjali (Kajol), the college best friend who quietly loved him before he married Tina (Mukerji), while Salman Khan plays Anjali’s fiancé.

No major Indian production before “Kuch Kuch Hota Hai” had shot as widely in Scotland. Johar’s unit filmed at Eilean Donan Castle, Glen Coe, Tantallon Castle and Inchmahome Priory, and the Scottish scenery became central to the film’s look. The film went on to forge a lasting link between the country’s landscapes and mainstream Indian cinema.

Other guests will also join the anniversary screening. Dates for the 2028 edition have yet to be announced.

“At EIFF we are always thinking about the future and what’s next. So we jumped at an opportunity like this, to plant the seeds for a celebration of a legendary, much-loved film at our festival, a film featuring Scotland and some of the most iconic stars of Bollywood cinema on screen. We can’t wait for what promises to be something truly special for our 81st edition in 2028. But in the meantime, watch this space for more news of our 80th next August,” said EIFF CEO and festival director Paul Ridd.

Before then, the festival will celebrate its 80th anniversary when it runs Aug. 12–18, 2027. Submissions for that edition open in January, and more details will follow in the coming months.

The milestone edition follows the festival’s revival in 2024 under Ridd and festival producer Emma Boa. EIFF is backed by Screen Scotland.

title_original: The 1973 ‘The Wicker Man’ Is a Classic, but Neil LaBute’s Loathed 2006 Remake Is Even Better
editorial_title_zh: 1973年的《异教徒》是一部经典，但尼尔·拉布特饱受诟病的2006年翻拍版甚至更好
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在万圣节周的“正确观点”（Correct Opinion）专栏中，我们来看看这部罕见的、超越原作的经典翻拍片——尽管你从影评中可听不到这种说法。

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "让人意外的是拉布特所拍恐怖片的类型和规模：一部由现成IP改编、大明星（尼尔森·凯奇）主演的好莱坞大制作。对于一位风格强烈且一向极具个人色彩的编剧兼导演来说，此前唯一的厂牌指派任务只有制作精良的文学改编作品《Possession》，《异教徒》似乎是一个奇怪的职业选择。", "links": [{"text": "The Wicker Man", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/the-wicker-man/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉布特当时只是破产了，还是将他自己的关切注入了安东尼·沙弗（Anthony Shaffer）的故事中？故事讲述了一名警探在偏远岛屿上调查失踪人口，最终走向末日。我不知道他是否需要这笔片酬，但我知道第二个问题的答案是一个响亮的“是”。《异教徒》不仅彻头彻尾地带有拉布特的个人风格，而且就像布赖恩·德帕玛的《疤面煞星》、约翰·卡彭特的《怪形》或大卫·柯南伯格的《苍蝇》一样，它是一部罕见的、实际上超越了其素材的经典翻拍片。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当时人们可不这么认为。拉布特的这部电影在票房上未能收回成本，几乎招致了影评人的一致鄙视，他们大多将其与原作进行不利的对比（顺便忘记了原作在上映时本身也遭遇了褒贬不一的评价）。拉布特获得了金酸莓奖最差剧本提名，考虑到金酸莓奖一贯擅长站在历史的对立面，单凭这一点就该成为该片品质的标志。（多年来该奖项的其他提名者还包括布莱克·爱德华兹、奥利弗·斯通、伊莲·梅、诺曼·梅勒和劳伦斯·卡斯丹。）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正如常见的那样，《异教徒》之所以出色，恰恰在于其狂野的基调混合，而这也正是它被误解的原因。那些没看懂这部电影的人的普遍共识是，它愚蠢而做作，尼古拉斯·凯奇的表演过于夸张，他穿着熊服潜入邪教仪式的场景简直荒谬。凯奇在片中的表演确实很夸张，那套熊服也很好笑。但这凭什么意味着这部电影做错了什么呢？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "恰恰相反，拉布特和凯奇显然非常清楚自己在做什么，影片的力量来自于真实恐怖感与一层顽皮黑色幽默之间的碰撞——这与拉布特广受赞誉的处女作《恶男别闹》具有相同的组合。那也是一部在不合时宜的地方引发笑声的电影，但拉布特作为一名没有公司支持的无名小卒，得到了观众的宽容。出于某种原因，当他在一部主流大制片厂电影中做同样的事情时，人们却将这些特质视为“错误”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/MCDWIMA_EC020.jpg?w=650", "alt": "《异教徒》，埃伦·伯斯廷（远左）、凯特·贝汉（中，手持兔子面具），©Warner Bros./courtesy Everett Collection", "caption": "《异教徒》©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection", "credit": "IndieWire", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "事实是，从像《塑造之物》这样的“纯粹”拉布特电影到《异教徒》，正如从《恶男别闹》到《你的朋友和邻居》一样，存在着一条直接的脉络。拉布特不只是重现1973年的电影；他以使其更具个人色彩、更复杂且更具共鸣的方式对其进行了重塑。关键的改动在于：凯奇饰演的警察前往了一个由女性社会主导的岛屿。这是一个简单的改变，但它让拉布特得以延续和发展对异性恋关系中权力动态变化的探讨，这一探讨始于他的第一部电影，并贯穿了他所写过的几乎每一部电影和戏剧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "自拉布特出道以来一直伴随他的对厌女症的持久指控是如此论据拙劣，以至于几乎不值得为其正名。它们大体上源于这样一种观点：既然拉布特的作品中男性对女性很刻薄，那么作品本身一定就是厌女的。反驳这一论点的最快方法就是简单地观看《恶男别闹》和《你的朋友和邻居》，并问一个简单的问题：在这些电影中，谁的形象最差？剧透：不是女性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "虽然《塑造之物》中的确塑造了一个在冰冷残忍方面几乎超自然的女性，但结合拉布特的其他作品来看，我认为与其说他是厌女症患者，不如说他是个厌世者和冷世者。我还想说，鉴于雷切尔·韦斯（Rachel Weisz）角色的艺术家身份，《塑造之物》既是一幅刻薄的自我画像，也是对女性的一种表态——这部电影是拉布特对艺术家如何为了艺术创作而将个人生活及爱人的剥削合理化这一现象的最有力审视。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不可否认，“异教徒”确实是该导演在抵御厌女症指控时最具挑战性的一部电影，但片中对女性操纵欲和利己主义的刻画，与影片对男性优越感及其焦虑的、往往极为搞笑的处理方式形成了平衡。就像原作中的警探一样，尼古拉斯·凯奇刚到岛上时，也带着性别和职位赋予他的傲慢权威，而拉布特则毫不掩饰地乐于在接下来的时间里剥夺凯奇的力量、安全感和理智。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/MCDWIMA_EC042.jpg?w=650", "alt": "“异教徒”，尼古拉斯·凯奇（左），2006年。©Warner Bros./courtesy Everett Collection", "caption": "“异教徒” ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection", "credit": "IndieWire", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这与拉布特对1973年电影所做的另一个重大改动有关：从一开始就将凯奇塑造成一个麻烦缠身、饱受妥协的角色。在原作中，爱德华·伍德沃德将警探饰演为一个笃信宗教的顾家好男人，其自我正义感似乎多多少少具有正当性。虽然当岛民嘲弄和折磨他时，这种设定形成了更鲜明的对比，但也让电影变得不那么细腻、有趣。凯奇到岛上时已经是一团糟——女性只是利用了潜藏在虚假男性自信外表之下的东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉布特对重点的转换，使得他的“异教徒”比1973年的原作更加复杂且引人入胜（尽管原作同样出色）。其次是电影制作功底的问题。几乎以任何标准来看，2006年的“异教徒”在美学上都比导演罗宾·哈迪令人不安但略显朴素的原作要丰富得多，其灯光和构图都极为精致。（该片获得的少数赞誉之一，便是加拿大电影摄影师协会授予摄影指导保罗·萨罗西的奖项。）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉布特从未真正获得应有的风格大师地位，这可能是因为他的处女作“男人公司”颗粒感堪比篮球大小，运镜极少，甚至让常规的“好汉两个半”都显得像是“不羁夜”一样。先入为主的印象根深蒂固，“男人公司”留下的印象是一个伟大的编剧，而其导演风格基本上只是把摄影机对准演员的大致方向，以便记录他们台词的交付。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但拉布特当时才刚刚热身。在25,000美元的制作预算下，“男人公司”是一部野心远远超出其资源的电影，而这位导演再也不会拍出技术上如此凌乱的电影了。他的下一部作品“阁楼男女”预算适中，为500万美元，但这让拉布特得以采用宽银幕拍摄，并在色彩、调度和节奏上倾注了精准的关怀。作为戈达尔“蔑视”的公开崇拜者，拉布特在随后的几乎所有作品中，都在形式上的优雅方面与该片一较高下。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这在“异教徒”中绝对得到了体现，这部电影充分利用了其厂牌资源，营造出一个又一个经过精妙编排的画幅。不过归根结底，赋予这部电影力量的与其说是其视觉和听觉才华，不如说是其核心深处那种强烈的背叛感。原作中警探的最终命运完全是由经济需求驱动的——他是岛上为了农作物繁茂而必需的人祭。", article_text:
Reader, you have been lied to! Film history is littered with unfairly maligned classics, whether critics were too eager to review the making of rather than the finished product, or they suffered from underwhelming ad campaigns or general disinterest. Let’s revise our takes on some of these films from wrongheaded to the correct opinion .

When filmmaker Neil LaBute signed on to write and direct a remake of the 1973 horror film “ The Wicker Man ” in 2006, both his fans and his detractors were surprised. Not that LaBute would be making a horror movie — after all, “In the Company of Men,” “Your Friends and Neighbors,” and “The Shape of Things” were all horror movies in a sense, disturbing pageants of trauma and sadism where the (human) monsters always won.

The surprise came in the type and scale of horror movie LaBute was making: a big-budget Hollywood movie with a big star (Nicolas Cage) derived from preexisting IP. Coming from a fiercely personal writer/director whose only previous studio assignment had been the handsomely mounted literary adaptation “Possession,” “ The Wicker Man ” seemed like an odd career choice.

Was LaBute just broke, or did he inject his own preoccupations into Anthony Shaffer’s tale of a policeman whose missing-person investigation on a remote island leads to his doom? I don’t know if he needed the payday, but I do know that the answer to the second half of the question was a resounding “yes.” Not only is “The Wicker Man” pure LaBute through and through, but it’s also, like Brian De Palma’s “Scarface,” John Carpenter’s “The Thing,” or David Cronenberg’s “The Fly,” a rare remake of a classic that’s actually superior to its source.

Not that people thought so at the time. LaBute’s movie failed to make its money back at the box office and drew almost universal scorn from critics, most of whom compared it unfavorably with the original (conveniently forgetting that the original itself met with mixed reviews upon release). LaBute was nominated for a Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Screenplay, which in and of itself should be a marker of the film’s quality given the Razzies’ consistent knack for being on the wrong side of history. (Other nominees in that category over the years have included Blake Edwards, Oliver Stone, Elaine May, Norman Mailer, and Lawrence Kasdan.)

As is so often the case, one of the very things that makes “The Wicker Man” great — its wild mix of tones — is also what made it misunderstood. The general consensus among those who didn’t get the movie was that it was silly and histrionic, that Nicolas Cage’s performance was over the top, and that scenes like the one where he infiltrates a cultish ceremony wearing a bear suit were ridiculous. Cage is over the top in the film, and the bear suit is funny. But why does this mean the movie is doing something wrong?

To the contrary, LaBute and Cage clearly know exactly what they’re doing, and the movie’s power comes from the collision between a sense of genuine horror and a layer of playful black comedy — the same combo that characterized LaBute’s acclaimed debut, “In the Company of Men.” That’s also a movie where laughs come in inappropriate places, but Labute got the benefit of the doubt as an unknown with no corporate support. For some reason, when he does the same thing in a major studio movie, people view the idiosyncrasies as “mistakes.”

The fact is that there’s as direct a line from a “pure” LaBute movie like “The Shape of Things” to “The Wicker Man” as there was from “In the Company of Men” to “Your Friends and Neighbors.” LaBute doesn’t just recreate the 1973 film; he reinvents it in ways that make it both more personal and more complex and resonant. The key alteration is that Cage’s cop character travels to an island dominated by a society of women. It’s a simple change, but it lets Labute extend and develop the inquiry into shifting power dynamics in heterosexual relationships that began with his first film and pervades nearly every film and play he ever wrote.

The persistent charges of misogyny that have followed LaBute since the beginning are so poorly argued they’re barely worth dignifying. They largely seem to stem from the idea that because men are mean to women in LaBute’s work, the work itself must be misogynistic. The quickest way to counter the argument is to simply watch “In the Company of Men” and “Your Friends and Neighbors” and ask one simple question: Who comes off most badly in these movies? Spoiler: It’s not the women.

While “The Shape of Things” does feature a woman who’s almost supernatural in her icy cruelty, taken in context alongside LaBute’s other work, I’d argue that if anything he’s a misanthrope and a cynic, not a misogynist. I’d also argue that given the Rachel Weisz character’s status as a kind of artist, “The Shape of Things” is as much a lacerating self-portrait as it is a statement about women — the movie is LaBute’s most potent examination of the ways in which artists justify the exploitation of their personal lives and their loved ones for the sake of their work.

“The Wicker Man” is admittedly the director’s most challenging film when it comes to defending him against the accusations of misogyny, but the view of women as manipulative and self-interested is counterbalanced by the movie’s often hilarious take on male superiority and anxiety. Like the detective in the original film, Cage arrives on the island puffed up with the authority his gender and position have given him, and LaBute takes undeniable pleasure in spending the rest of the movie stripping Cage of his power, security, and sanity.

This connects to another of LaBute’s big changes from the 1973 film: making Cage a troubled, compromised soul from the start. In the original movie, Edward Woodward plays the cop as a religious family man whose self-righteousness seems more or less justified. While this creates a starker contrast as the island residents taunt and torment him, it also makes for a less nuanced, interesting movie. Cage is already a mess when he gets to the island — the women just exploit what is already lying in wait beneath the phony masculine confidence on the surface.

LaBute’s shifts in emphasis make his “Wicker Man” more complex and rewarding than the 1973 film, effective as it is. Then there’s the question of filmmaking prowess. By virtually any standard, the 2006 “Wicker Man” is simply a far more aesthetically rich movie than director Robin Hardy’s unsettling but somewhat plain original, exquisitely lit and composed. (Among the movie’s few accolades was an award for DP Paul Sarossy from the Canadian Society of Cinematographers.)

LaBute has never really gotten his due as a stylist, possibly because his debut feature, “In the Company of Men,” had grain the size of basketballs and so little camera movement it made a routine episode of “Two and a Half Men” look like “Boogie Nights.” First impressions stick, and the impression “In the Company of Men” left behind was that of a great writer whose directorial style was basically just aiming the camera in the general direction of the actors to record them delivering his dialogue.

But LaBute was just getting warmed up. Shot on a production budget of $25,000, “In the Company of Men” was a film whose ambitions far outstripped its resources, and its director would never make a movie as technically ramshackle again. His follow-up, “Your Friends & Neighbors,” was modestly budgeted at $5 million but enabled LaBute to shoot in ‘scope and with precise care when it came to color, blocking, and rhythm. A professed admirer of Godard’s “Contempt,” LaBute would go on to rival that film’s formal elegance in virtually everything he made afterward.

That’s certainly true of “The Wicker Man,” a movie that fully utilizes its studio resources to create one expertly orchestrated frame after another. In the end, though, what gives the film its power is less its visual and aural flair than the deep sense of betrayal at its core. The cop’s ultimate fate in the original is motivated purely by economic necessity — he’s a human sacrifice the island needs for its crops to flourish.

This is true of the remake as well, but LaBute’s changes to Cage’s character, and his addition of a personal connection to the island, add a chilling dimension the original lacks. The movie’s final moments carry the same authentic sense of horror found in the betrayals that climax “In the Company of Men” and “The Shape of Things,” and the reversal is perhaps even more powerful coming in the form of an ostensibly commercial, mainstream movie.

Like Martin Scorsese’s “Cape Fear” or Spike Lee’s “Inside Man,” “The Wicker Man” is a genre movie given added potency by its filmmaker’s uncompromising sense of personal commitment. It also hints at what was to come in LaBute’s career, as he would ultimately lean into his knack for genre filmmaking — in recent years, all his movies have been thrillers or horror pictures, albeit with far fewer resources than “The Wicker Man.” “The Wicker Man” remains an artistic, if not commercial or critical, high point. Now that it just turned 20, maybe it’s time people finally acknowledged its virtues.
excerpt_original: In a Halloween-week edition of the "Correct Opinion" column, we take a look at a rare remake of a classic that's superior to the original — not that you would have known it from the reviews.

article_text:
Lucca Comics and Games director Emanuele Vietina is understandably proud of the lineup he’s assembled for the 60th edition of this unique event, to be held Oct. 28-Nov. 1 in the Tuscan town of Lucca, which seamlessly spans the full gamut of geek culture and pop entertainment.

It also attracts more than 200,000 fans a day – many of which cosplayers – within its medieval ramparts.

Related Stories

Sylvester Stallone Says Daughter’s ‘Tulsa King’ Casting Is ‘Of Course’ Nepotism: ‘Obviously We Let Them Have Every Advantage’

Korea Box Office: Anime Phenomenon 'Chiikawa' Remains Unstoppable as Yeon Sang-ho Thriller 'Paradise Lost' Debuts

As previously announced, highlights of this year’s edition include a sneak peak of Season 3 of “ Percy Jackson and the Olympians,” with talents in tow and the presence of Aardman Animations’ founder Peter Lord and director Peter Walker for the Italian premiere of “Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom.” In a major coup, Japanese filmmaker Kore-eda Hirokazu will be making the trek to Lucca to meet fans and discuss adapting Fujimoto Tatsuki’s manga “Look Back,” which blends live-action realism with the creative process behind the manga genre. To mark its 60th anniversary, Lucca will feature “Lucca Legacy: A Comics and Games Story” exhibition in the 14th century Palazzo Guinigi, which will dig into the archival vaults to “tell a seminal story that was made by [Marvel legend] Stan Lee, [‘Iron Man,’ ‘Black Panther’ and ‘The X-Men’] creator Jack Kirby, [iconic Hearst cartoonist] Lee Falk and all the great American artists comics that found a home in Lucca in the 70s,” says Vietina.

The Lucca Comics chief speaks to Variety about pulling out all the stops to celebrate the crossover between different forms of geek culture, in particular between movies and video games.

Popular on Variety

The “Legacy” theme represents, if you will, the heritage of what has become one of the world’s major comic conventions. The way film and TV series at Lucca engage with the great fantasy storytelling of Percy Jackson is that the book’s author, Rick Riordan, is essentially bringing things up to date. We often talk about “contemporary mythology.” With Percy Jackson, which features Olympus and the Olympian gods, he revitalizes the great heritage of classical Greco-Roman culture, making it accessible to young people today.

An event like ours deals with contemporary mythologies, yet it remains firmly anchored in the mythology of the past. This year, however, is particularly emblematic. For the movie world, Lucca is not merely the oldest comics convention in existence, or even the only one to feature a formal red carpet in front of an opera house that dates back to the turn of the 20th century.

On top of these aspects, we will also have a special fan screening of “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” which is the latest entry in the “Hunger Games” film franchise, based on Suzanne Collins’ 2025 novel. Warner Bros. will bring the world of “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone” [known as “Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone” in the U.S.] to Lucca in an immersive pavilion while we wait for the new HBO series. So with Riordan, Collins and J. K. Rowling, Lucca will become, above all, the realm where great literature meets great cinema.

Another aspect that characterizes Lucca is the exhibition side. In Lucca, we have the big premieres with talents, but there are also big stands for fans. So “Percy Jackson” will have a dedicated experience space, the same goes with “Harry Potter,” but there is also “Dexter” and others. This year we have set the all-time record of investments from the studios and streamers.

There is plenty of room for the world of cosplay, with a particular focus on crossovers between the cinematic realm and the video game world. We’ll see a significant presence from [Polish video game developer] CD Projekt Red, featuring “Cyberpunk 2077” and the “Cyberpunk Edgerunners” animation, as well as “The Witcher,” which will be represented alongside its latest downloadable content (DLC). It’s clear that this European studio has truly embraced the crossover concept, especially given the news surrounding a cinematic expansion for “Cyberpunk 2077.”

For us, the strong focus that Lucca Comics and Games places on video games, specifically from a cinematic perspective, is very important. In this context, I want to point out that we will have Hideki Kamiya [the legendary game director behind “ Resident Evil 2 ,” “Devil May Cry” and “Okami”], and also [director and producer] Yoshinori Kitase, who will revitalize the connection with Square Enix and the “Final Fantasy” fan base. Then there is the presence of the creators of “Alien: Isolation 2,” a game that is very strongly driven by movies. It’s all part of a specific vision.

In terms of legacy, this 60th edition of Lucca marks a great return to a major focus on animation. I’ve already mentioned CD Projekt Red, with Bartosz Sztybor and Saya Elder, who are the producer and showrunner of “Edgerunners” coming to Lucca. Just as importantly, we have [Cartoon Network Studio’s] “Adventure Time” with one of its co-creators Victor Cartwright on hand. Then we will have Aardman Animations represented by its founder Peter Lord. They will be coming for the Italian premiere of “Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom.” Lord, who, of course, is beloved by everyone, will be honored on our “Walk of Fame,” as he represents one of the most significant legacies in the field. He’ll be joined by Matthew Walker, the film’s director. For us, Peter’s presence is truly meaningful.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

article_text:
It’s late January, and the intrepid Film Comment crew is on the ground reporting from an extra special edition of the Sundance Film Festival—the last to take place on the snowy slopes of Park City, Utah, the festival’s home since 1981, before moving to Boulder, Colorado in 2027. For the next week, we’ll be gathering the best critics on the scene to talk about each day’s premieres on the Podcast.

For our second Podcast from the fest, Film Comment Editor Devika Girish sat down with programmer Madeline Whittle (Film at Lincoln Center) and critic Will Tavlin ( n+1 ) to discuss Adam and Zack Khalil’s Aanikoobijigan [ancestor/great-grandparent/great-grandchild] (1:54), John Wilson’s The History of Concrete (14:05), and Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman’s Nuisance Bear (28:11).

article_text:
Trump Administration

Trump Proclaims Gold-Studded Oval Office a National Monument

"It will not be allowed to be touched by anybody,” Trump said, which is flatly not true, as anyone can reverse the proclamation.

Apparently scrambling to secure his legacy after the blue tsunami of midterm triumphs for Democrats, President Donald Trump proclaimed the White House's Oval Office, Outer Oval Office, and Cabinet Room a joint national monument on Thursday, November 3. The proclamation rests on the same historic preservation law the president invoked to significantly diminish two cultural sites in Utah earlier this year.

The proclamation is not legally binding, meaning a future president could simply reverse it. Trump has outfitted the Oval Office with gold frames and trim, Mar-a-Lago maximalism, and his approximations of Louis XIV's Palace of Versailles in an aesthetic that former President Barack Obama said looked like “Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” The president issued the proclamation under the Antiquities Act of 1906 , a law that lets presidents designate national monuments and protects archaeological and historical sites on federal lands.

While the Antiquities Act does not give presidents the authority to reduce, alter, or raze national monuments, Trump invoked the law in 2017 to shrink the boundaries of the Grand Staircase-Escalante and Bears Ears , two national monuments in Southern Utah that encompass culturally significant Indigenous lands. President Joe Biden restored the national monuments to their original size, though Trump doubled down in his second presidential term by reducing both sites by approximately 90% each this July.

article_text:
ストレンジ・リトル・キャット

劇場公開日： 2026年10月30日

映画館を探す

予告編を見る

U-NEXTで 関連作品を見る PR

解説・あらすじ

スイス出身でドイツにて映画制作を学んだ双子の映画作家ラモン＆シルバン・チュルヒャー兄弟が2013年に発表し、世界各地の映画祭で注目を集めた長編デビュー作。「ガール・アンド・スパイダー」「煙突の中の雀」へと連なる「動物三部作」の第1作。 カリンは両親と幼い妹クララが暮らすベルリンのアパートを訪れる。夜には親戚たちも集まり、夕食をともにする予定だ。洗濯機の修理を待ち、台所のテーブルを囲み、オレンジの皮を使って実験をする。猫と犬が室内を歩きまわり、人々は出入りを繰り返す。特別なことは何も起こらないが、小さな行為が次の行為を呼び、ひとつの言葉が別の言葉へと連なっていくうちに、家族の平凡な1日は奇妙で精密な連鎖反応へと変化していく。 ラモンが監督・脚本・編集・サウンドデザインを手がけ、シルバンが製作を担当。2013年・第63回ベルリン国際映画祭フォーラム部門にて初上映。2025年・第26回東京フィルメックス上映作品。2026年10月、「ガール・アンド・スパイダー」「煙突の中の雀」とともに「ミニアチュールの詩学 チュルヒャー兄弟『動物三部作』」と題して劇場公開。

2013年製作／72分／G／ドイツ 原題または英題：Das Merkwurdige Katzchen 配給：グッチーズ・フリースクール 劇場公開日：2026年10月30日

title_original: Patrick Stewart brought gravitas and complexity to the screen, from Star Trek to X-Men
editorial_title_zh: 帕特里克·斯图尔特为银幕带来庄严与复杂，从《星际迷航》到《X战警》
editorial_excerpt_zh: 从让-吕克·皮卡尔到查尔斯·泽维尔，这位演员的莎剧训练——以及那磁性的嗓音——使他成为好莱坞独特的魅力化身 帕特里克·斯图尔特逝世，享年86岁 他的生平影像集 哦，船长，我们的船长：在《星际迷航》中，帕特里克·斯图尔特能让任何人感受到……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "没有哪位演员能像帕特里克·斯图尔特那样，展现出英国顶级古典表演训练的商业潜力。凭借风格、技巧以及极其敏锐、几乎带有滑稽剧色彩的模仿力，莎剧演员能够驾驭美国电影和高端美剧，向美国演技派演员展示什么是真正的专业——有时甚至在他们银幕生涯之初，就以极具竞争力的低片酬做到这一点。", "links": [{"text": "Patrick Stewart", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/culture/patrick-stewart"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "斯图尔特是皇家莎士比亚剧团20世纪70年代舞台演出世代的翘楚，此前他也曾出演过高水准的小荧幕角色，例如他在《我，克劳狄乌斯》中与德里克·雅各比搭档，饰演令人望而生畏的塞亚努斯。但他通过在电视剧《星际迷航：下一代》中饰演联邦星舰企业号船长让-吕克·皮卡尔，实现了向流行文化超级巨星的跃升。《星际迷航：下一代》是《星际迷航》极其成功重启之作，从1987年一直播到1994年，催生了4部独立电影以及随后的另一部剧集《星际迷航：皮卡尔》。", "links": [{"text": "Star Trek", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/culture/star-trek"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "斯图尔特身材健硕、气场强大、声如洪钟——而且是个光头（不过带有一种独特的阳刚之气）。威廉·夏特纳饰演的詹姆斯·T·柯克船长更像是太空探索世界里形象清爽的肯尼迪式人物、动作浪漫片男主角，但斯图尔特饰演的皮卡尔则是一个更复杂的角色，在精神上——凭借其异国情调的名字和光头——稍微更接近那些作为星际多元《星际迷航》演员阵容常规元素的异星人物和本土星球居民。（艾伦·瑞克曼在1999年太空喜剧《银河系漫游指南》中饰演的傲慢演员转变为科幻偶像的亚历山大·戴恩，或许多少受到了斯图尔特的启发。）新一代的星际迷航粉丝（Trekkers）找到了一位充满魅力的全新领袖来追随。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/4fa54ef867a19cad3b77ed2d7e6a7e6452d4558f/0_0_2610_1738/master/2610.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "帕特里克·斯图尔特在2002年《星际迷航：复仇女神》中饰演让-吕克·皮卡尔", "caption": "“新一代的星际迷航粉丝找到了一位充满魅力的全新领袖来追随”……帕特里克·斯图尔特在2002年电影《星际迷航：复仇女神》中。照片：Globe Photos/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在取得了这一非凡的成功之后，斯图尔特又征服了超级英雄的世界；他将自己在《星际迷航》中积聚的流行文化资本转移到了漫威电影宇宙中。随着00年代初漫威品牌开始其庞大的票房统治地位，斯图尔特在《X战警》系列中饰演了坐在轮椅上的尊贵人物——查尔斯·泽维尔教授（Professor Charles Xavier），即X教授，成为了多厅影院的性格演员兼巨星。作为泽维尔，斯图尔特与饰演万磁王的伊恩·麦克莱恩演对手戏，后者是另一位皇家莎士比亚剧团的巨星，他以良好的幽默感穿上莱卡紧身衣，并以铿锵有力的信念念出台词。事实上，泽维尔教授这个变种人导师和引路人的角色，可能让斯图尔特更多地汲取了其莎士比亚戏剧背景：作为泽维尔，他常常流露出一种睿智而有王者风范的神情，特别是当该系列将他描绘成某种流亡君主的时候。", "links": [{"text": "X-Men", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/x-men"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "必须指出的是，斯图尔特在此之前就在科幻和奇幻领域有过不少演艺经历。他是约翰·保曼充满远见的1981年电影《黑暗时代》中吉娜维芙的父亲勒多格兰斯国王，也是大卫·林奇独特版本的弗兰克·赫伯特1984年《沙丘》中保罗·阿特雷迪斯的顾问哥尼·哈莱克。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/6603b502696b141678a5adb1cf3d3e38b0c8557c/0_0_2396_1601/master/2396.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "帕特里克·斯图尔特与伊恩·麦克莱恩相对而坐，两人之间摆着一盘国际象棋", "caption": "斯图尔特与伊恩·麦克莱恩在2000年《X战警》中演对手戏。照片：20thC.Fox/Everett/Shutterstock", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
N o actor showed the commercial potential of blue-chip British classical training like Patrick Stewart . With style, technique and the most minutely self-aware, almost vaudevillian sense of mimicry, Shakespearean thesps can turn their hand to American movies and high-end American television and show the American method actors how it’s done – sometimes, even, at the beginning of their screen careers, at a competitively low wage.

Stewart was one of the thoroughbreds of the Royal Shakespeare Company’s 1970s stage generation who had also had classy small screen roles, such as his intimidating Sejanus in I, Claudius opposite Derek Jacobi. But he effected a warp-speed leap to pop culture stardom by getting the role of Jean-Luc Picard, captain of the Federation starship USS Enterprise, in TV’s Star Trek: The Next Generation, the hugely successful reboot of Star Trek that ran from 1987 to 1994, spawning four separate feature films and then another series, Star Trek: Picard.

Stewart was athletic, commanding, sonorous – and bald (though in a distinctively virile way). William Shatner’s Captain James Kirk had been a more clean-cut JFK of the space-exploration world, an action-romantic lead, but Stewart’s Picard was a more complex figure, slightly nearer in spirit – with that exotic name of his and the hairless head – to the alien figures and indigenous planet-dwellers who were now a regular feature of intergalactically diverse Star Trek cast. (Alan Rickman’s haughty actor turned sci-fi icon Alexander Dane in the 1999 space comedy Galaxy Quest was perhaps a little inspired by Stewart.) A whole new generation of Trekkers found a charismatic new leader to rally round.

And with that remarkable coup in the bag, Stewart went on to conquer the world of superhero-dom; he transferred the pop-culture capital he had amassed in Star Trek to the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Stewart became a character-actor-slash-star of the multiplex as the wheelchair-using eminence Professor Charles Xavier, or Professor X, in the X-Men franchise at the beginning of the 00s as the Marvel brand began its colossal box-office dominance. As Xavier, Stewart played opposite Ian McKellen as Magneto, that other RSC Galactico who good-humouredly wore the Lycra and delivered the lines with resounding conviction. And in fact the role of Professor Xavier, the mentor and tutor to the mutants, probably allowed Stewart to draw even more on his Shakespearean background: he often had a wise and kingly mien as Xavier, especially when the franchise showed him as a kind of exiled monarch.

It should be said that Stewart had some form in sci-fi and fantasy way before this. He was Guenevere’s father, King Leodegrance, in John Boorman’s visionary Excalibur in 1981 and the adviser to Paul Atreides, Gurney Halleck, in David Lynch’s distinctive version of Frank Herbert’s Dune in 1984.

But for me his most satisfying non-franchise movie role, and the one that allowed him to be vehemently and compellingly bad in a way Star Trek and Marvel didn’t, was Jeremy Saulnier’s horror-thriller Green Room , in which Stewart plays a neo-Nazi leader who, along with his brutish rank and file, tries to attack a rock band who have barricaded themselves into the green room of the scuzzy bar they’ve just played and where they have discovered something awful.

Stewart’s face could transform into a threatening mask: he could look handsome and refined but also leonine and aggressive, and the mellifluous voice could deliver a nasal edge of threat. Stewart was a unique charismatic force on screen.

title_original: 想像一個不屬於她的世界──專訪《有用的人》導演李芸嬋
title_zh: 想像一個不屬於她的世界──專訪《有用的人》導演李芸嬋
summary_zh: 来源摘录：《有用的人》淺白地講述家庭成員各自的困境，卻未見角色做出選擇時的掙扎，李芸嬋將之稱作「節制」，她認為環境、空間會替角色說話，表演也會替角色說話。而母親角色的最後呈現，是角色、演員與導演，她們同樣生為女人、作為母親，「我希望母親有別的選擇，意識到自己的生命需要其他的出路，她不能繼續被困在家裡了。」 這篇文章 想像一個不屬於她的世界──專訪《有用的人》導演李芸嬋 最早出現於 釀電影 。

Ordinary，2026）的時間跨度很長，而此處所指的時間，它既是李芸嬋將十多年來的生活見聞凝鍊於電影中，也是李芸嬋作為導演、作為一對子女的母親，她透過電影裡的女兒的成長，想要看見生活裡變了又變、一變再變的事物。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "首先，是關於家變。電影開場，觀眾很快地會看到一個普通家庭急轉直下的命運：好不容易讀了大學，可以一面打工支撐自己的生活開銷，突如其來的車禍，卻將青年的夢、一個家庭的夢給撞碎了。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其後的變化，在電影裡迅速翻頁：車禍，復健，戀愛，生病，死亡；升學，離職，離婚，出走，出走，再出走。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "跑馬燈般匆匆流逝的人物生活，我們不免在離場之際想起幾次驚鴻，接著就是蒼白的記憶，觀眾似乎只能記得事件，而難以體察特定角色的心境流轉；藉由景物帶來人物的變化，《有用的人》一下子帶領觀眾去到十幾年後，這不免有些飄搖，就像我們在玩那個名為《八十億分之一》的模擬人生遊戲，生命一直都是晃眼就過。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "遊戲玩家可以透過星號註記生命中難以忘懷的記憶，遊戲則編年地記述生命裡特別大、彷彿注定般的事物，比如出生在兒童致死率較高的國家、成長在特別貧窮的家庭、某年的世界疫病帶走了妳／你的家人、似乎到了適婚年紀而妳／你決定繼續升學等。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "當然，它還有一些特別小的事物，像是媽媽煮了一道家常料理、奶奶與妳／你講起家族的古老故事、妳／你在下班途中看見了一抹晚霞⋯⋯，而在玩家死亡之後，遊戲會帶領玩家回顧生命中的重要時刻，就像射擊遊戲總會慢動作回放精準獵殺的剎那，《八十億分之一》會留下那些巨大的轉折，與妳／你主動註記的、或大或小的事物。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "於是在《有用的人》散場之後，觀眾可能記起的情節也將有所不同，且會隨著觀眾自身的家庭位置，而有不同的關注目光。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/F5YVeLn14deSJOJyZUT2wuYw8xAqkNVMU_UUkLNF42c/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/bb5503ae-deec-4c0e-b989-af2249458e3d.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》導演李芸嬋專訪。／專訪攝影：ioauue", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》導演李芸嬋專訪。／專訪攝影：ioauue"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/NLShuecxsaIW06AOKCsKdO-psIGt9D2k_m_0BPqSIhc/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/b2e8a12c-c949-4172-8e31-bec3a53b1def.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "關於時間的推移，電影裡的妹妹一角尤為代表。國小教室，妹妹正學習自然科學知識；國中放學，妹妹獨自在嶄新的電梯公寓煮食；晾曬著高中制服的空鏡頭，再過不久就要大學畢業、步入社會了。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "李芸嬋沒有玩過《八十億分之一》，但她這十幾年來的生活，就像模擬人生似的，不斷地採集他人的故事，「那些讓我感到震驚，但我不一定理解、也未曾經驗過的事物，我一直把它們收著，擺進我的資料夾裡。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此處值得留意的，比起許多創作者會使用的「抽屜」一詞，李芸嬋的用字是「資料夾」；這些來自他人生命的事物，可能是按照它的屬性、標籤，依序分類進她的世界。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因為這樣的採集過程，讓《有用的人》從一開始就沒有具體前進的方向，可以說是李芸嬋把那本累積了十多年的資料夾，全灑進這次的故事裡了。 這樣的創作理路，不僅一口氣收攏十年光陰，還交錯多種議題、錯落多道目光，光是敘事本身的駁雜，的確已經讓不少觀眾、評論者感到遲疑。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不過李芸嬋仍認為，這是她一開始就決定好的。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/F9t3efOZSLkc0XoapEl4Cx9C8azw3uzBJkXhepZI4MA/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/f844fc4d-6b02-41bd-99a5-c850a7c0bb1a.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/KbOw1SaVndRku7wJhkvXOlT8O1WqtDjJJ7kmL1wCH5g/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/659b1c6a-0867-49f1-8d0a-b2a5e6be4456.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會"}, {"type": "quote", "text": "「起初在組織故事時，我沒有結構。我只是把我關心的事情、我的疑問套進角色裡，聽聞了什麼、新聞裡又有什麼，我通通把它們寫進去。有時候寫媽媽、爸爸，偶爾也跳著寫妹妹、哥哥，有了一大堆素材之後，我才開始組織自己想說的事，我知道是「關係」。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "電影背景是大量臺商至中國設廠的多年之後，以住在臺北的中產階級故事伊始，李芸嬋想要呈現的是住在臺北的當代中產階級家庭關係，不過這裡可能有的差異，應該是階級的定義了。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "片中的肇事者，其子赴美留學後定居，退休外省老父在臺北獨居，除了自己住的那一幢房屋，還有另一戶出租中的新電梯大樓；遭逢家變的家庭，父親失業、母親為職業婦女，另有一名讀大學的兒子、小學高年級的女兒，一家四口租在一戶較舊的無電梯傳統公寓。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "即使李芸嬋將這兩個家庭皆稱之為中產階級，不過可以想見的是，後者大概沒有太多的餘裕，可以連串接招生活中大大小小的變故。這個意思是，如果不是電影，這家人不會有機會收到一幢新房子、每月八萬元（還沒有明確期限）的賠償費，家庭功能早在負擔龐大的照護、復健費用時，早早就被拖垮了。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/z5nFujmfFUFX2x981ZeT1T8W0d_Z6N0i5RsHtTeafc4/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/579740e3-fde5-4884-9607-60916b02ddc3.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》導演李芸嬋專訪。／專訪攝影：ioauue", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》導演李芸嬋專訪。／專訪攝影：ioauue"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/UdeEtFxEs6hYtIj6i31Y4DW3kjwn5aTdXwz_j4O0ATw/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/339bda83-5570-4682-bbdd-eb028d25d653.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》導演李芸嬋專訪。／專訪攝影：ioauue", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》導演李芸嬋專訪。／專訪攝影：ioauue"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "這是電影最不寫實的設計，也是唯有電影才能選擇的路徑，而李芸嬋透過如此的綺想，想要看見的是其中之於夫妻、子女、空間和時代的關係。"}, {"type": "quote", "text": "「這樣的幸福背後，是不是其實很脆弱？當無常發生時，我們會做出什麼選擇？生活在臺北這樣的都市裡，我很難用單一視角講故事，這沒有辦法讓我說我想說的事。所以我採用比較客觀的觀點，讓每個人都可以平均被看見。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "同樣拍攝家庭故事的臺灣電影 《我家的事》（Family Matters，2025） ，分幕式地帶出家庭成員各自的生活樣態，而《有用的人》選擇將家庭成員各自的生命時間平行剪輯，且聚焦於家庭共同經驗的大事。", "links": [{"text": "《我家的事》（Family Matters，2025）", "url": "https://filmaholic.tw/interview/68e28b38fd89780001c25c7a/"}]}, {"type": "quote", "text": "「因為劇本的時間跨度很長，所以在故事結構出來之後，劇組接著思考的是如何透過技術，讓觀眾知道時間的流逝。只不過第一版劇本寫完後，有很多人跟我說不知道故事的主角是誰，也不知道該跟著誰的情緒去走，所以我也嘗試過只聚焦在特定一人的觀點，看看能不能繼續發展故事。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "面對同樣的家變，爸爸的應對許是沉默卻也順應生命的哀慟，媽媽則困囚於自身的追悔與執著，而妹妹卻是介於兩者之外，她只能做出感受性的選擇，像是體恤家變的辛勞，或者感到被遺棄。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "李芸嬋發現自己沒有辦法只用單一觀點，比起一個人的長成，她想知道的是事件帶來的影響，而電影最後的呈現，其實就像是我們在翻讀李芸嬋的一本資料夾，那是她自己看待世界的方式，而這不一定和角色相關。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "所以這部電影的主角，李芸嬋明白是她自己。她依然是用自己的眼界，看待這些她的階級之外的事物，這也解釋了電影多採用較遠的鏡頭，彷彿在這個家庭裡有另一個人，並非以第五位家庭成員的視角，而僅僅是以苦難的局外人靜默觀之。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/NwFAgtcnagdILU99LSGFnBUrJHD8xT1m0G1qJI6F4Ao/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/ed72ee05-f608-4a25-96e6-62daa7dfabb9.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/H0vGRYmbtd-RSDOmoYlMRzr7G3DfvpWBfJvqy7kubVo/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/fe3cfc21-744f-42cf-acd6-b6b7efc6a686.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會"}, {"type": "quote", "text": "「如果我選擇的是全知觀點，那麼就沒有辦法只跟著單一角色的心境轉折，因此劇本所採用的是在這十年的時間線裡，某一個時間點、某一個事件，每個人的反應是什麼？我只看反應而已，但這麼做行不行得通，我自己其實也沒有把握，因為電影是經驗的故事，觀眾能不能感到共鳴，很仰賴自身的感性。所以我的電影只是容器，你可以把你家的事放進來，所有人的選擇都不可能是最正確的唯一解答，對吧？因為我們都是無用之人吧，那我們是不是可以更寬容一點？我的企圖是這樣。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》淺白地講述家庭成員各自的困境，卻未見角色做出選擇時的掙扎，只看見在選擇之後，其他的家庭成員又該如何繼續面對，李芸嬋將之稱作「節制」，她認為環境、空間會替角色說話，表演也會替角色說話。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「我覺得生活很模糊，選擇也總在一念之間，真要解釋人類的行為，其實又太複雜了。而每個角色會產生什麼樣的漣漪，其實就在演員和角色之間的距離，我們不需要教演員做任何事情。」 比如，在電影中後段，楊祐寧飾演的爸爸一角，在陌生的計程車司機面前，終於道出兒子已逝、自己卻還持續領收每月的生活補償，李芸嬋只要楊祐寧想著角色十年間的經過，而不特別要求演員要做出什麼樣的反應。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "或者，在飾演哥哥的謝展榮身上，李芸嬋看見的是演員和角色相似的眼神，「你真的去拍他，你會知道他的眼神不只是那樣，他的心裡有很多事物一直在運作著。」而飾演妹妹一角的陳品嫙，李芸嬋也同樣在她的身上，看見了角色本身的特質，「在表演課上，有些孩子很會表演、表達，但是輪到陳品嫙的呈現時，她會問我是不是要跟著其他演員一樣哭。她是一直專注地在觀察別人的類型，妹妹在家裡也是這樣的角色。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "而在角色層次最複雜的母親一角，李芸嬋選擇在開拍之前，將母親角色的生命年表一一寫下，但張詩盈卻回頭問起：「媽媽到底是一個怎麼樣的人？」李芸嬋自承，起初她不曉得要怎麼回答，畢竟角色一生的年表，就洋洋灑灑地擺在面前了。 後來，她才知道張詩盈問的，是一個人的天性。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/o8PimfVixD2JJ5kLW8itCh2oJkbkJg-ToMx1jxFwQjo/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/1216d527-fd1d-4aa7-9dff-1bb72b6c12c4.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/ENWpurA7hb2cKGZP0QtXruRzzE386LWeL_Koy7cGZzQ/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/706bd3a3-16bd-4209-ae86-c11a22c8475a.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會"}, {"type": "quote", "text": "「在故事寫完之後，有人跟我說母親角色很『典型』，我一直在想這件事，然後想說：『有哪一個媽媽想成為典型的媽媽？如果不是被逼著做選擇，誰會想要成為典型的媽媽？』這樣的形象，或許不是多數人所想要的，因為她強悍、強勢，卻又要撐起家庭的苦難，而我們不能因為一個女人這樣子⋯⋯，就要求她永遠堅強、勇敢。」"}, {"type": "quote", "text": "「電影裡的兩場戲，一場戲是爸爸被身後掠過的藍鵲嚇到，另一場戲是媽媽看見在陽臺築巢的鴿子，然後她崩潰了。我在寫劇本時，想的是離開的孩子回來看爸爸媽媽了，只是他們不一定有力氣能接收到孩子捎來的訊號。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "李芸嬋認為，母親角色的最後呈現，已經是角色、演員與導演三者揉雜後的結果，而她們同樣生為女人、作為母親，角色最後的選擇卻又是李芸嬋的私心。 「我希望母親有別的選擇，意識到自己的生命需要其他的出路，她不能繼續被困在家裡了。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "李芸嬋的私心，其實同時也是她的天性使然。在她早期的電影創作中，多以魔幻題材關注與自身接近的故事，但是十年之後，她才慢慢意識到在自己的世界之外，有更多的脆弱、無常，與難以撼動的階級、無可避免的命運，總是大規模地發生在她的世界外緣。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但是她依然有自己的侷限，或許她也只能看見苦難的表面，更難以處理難解的生命關係。所以她能做的只有持續想像，李芸嬋依然在自己的奇幻世界裡面，想像不一樣的生命選擇，想像生命會不會有更好的出路，想像一個自己不曾經驗的世界。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/iqYftuQRRhUfDABnEdND03YxbVC_PgPCejclBmU0_MM/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/708a6369-3900-43c4-8fc7-c68b090b65dd.png", "alt": "《釀電影》，「如果月亮背面是汪洋，日光就是生命的海流──金馬 63 專題」主視覺。／圖像提供：釀電影（設計：林雅萱）", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《釀電影》，「如果月亮背面是汪洋，日光就是生命的海流──金馬 63 專題」主視覺。／圖像提供：釀電影（設計：林雅萱）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "月亮是最古早的電視，而電影百年的靈光， 是被迫倒下的巨樹身後，有眾人為祂記憶。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果月亮背面是汪洋， 日光就是生命的海流。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "↝↝↝【 閱讀 第 63 屆金馬獎專題 】↜↜↜", "links": [{"text": "閱讀 第 63 屆金馬獎專題", "url": "https://filmaholic.tw/covers/tghff2026/"}]}]
